answer: A stake that vests over time makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock collateral before it can earn, and the lock only unlocks after a long horizon of honest work. A Sybil attacker starting a fresh voyage with a thousand sock-puppets pays a thousand locks and waits the same slow release, while one real agent's reputation compounds. Every fake vote then sends a ripple of cost through the attacker's own capital instead of free influence.
